text:
maria: Quick follow-up on the demux vs unified-batcher tradeoffs we hashed out in the RFC. Need to pick an approach for cost attribution + rollout plan this week.
aj: TL;DR options?
maria: Option A: demux early — create per-tenant queues before batching. Pros: correct per-tenant cost accounting, easy to attach origin attrs. Cons: many queues, hot tenants create backpressure, more memory and routing complexity.
kevin: Option B: unified batcher with in-batch demuxing (tag batches with tenant keys). Pros: better GPU utilization, fewer queues, simpler scheduling. Cons: attribution delayed until late-enrich, harder to backfill/charge correctly.
sophia: Another hybrid: demux at coarse groups (tiered tenants) + unified batching inside each tier. Fewer queues than per-tenant but still limits hotspots.
tarun: Important interface question: what does the edge produce? Right now edge emits envelope with minimal attrs: {billing_key, tenant_id?, sample_ratio?}. If we rely on late-enrich we need deterministic, unambiguous billing_key before enrichment.
maria: Agree. We need a contract: ingest -> envelope must contain either billing_key OR a stable tenant_id plus provenance headers we can map later. No partials.
aj: If we go unified, we must ensure the enrich pipeline has an idempotent, low-latency mapping to billing_key. Late mapping is okay if we can attach attribution atomically and re-emit cost events.
kevin: Hotspot mitigation: even with unified batcher we should cap max per-tenant tokens per batch and enforce per-tenant in-flight windows. Otherwise a single tenant can dominate a batch.
sophia: Also consider metrics surface: we need per-batch telemetry exposing tenant_count, dominant_tenant_share, tokens_per_tenant_p95. Ops needs that before we roll.
tarun: Example minimal config we'd need on ingest:
``` 
ingest:
  demux_enabled: false
  batch_window_ms: 25
  max_tokens_per_tenant: 2000
  required_keys: ["billing_key", "tenant_id"]
```
maria: Rollout plan proposal:
- Phase 0 (canary): deploy unified batcher with demux_enabled=false to 2 non-critical regions. Emit per-batch metrics + sampling of batch payloads (anonymized).
- Phase 1 (observability): run for 48h, validate attribution accuracy against legacy demuxed accounting. Gate: <1% mismatch and no sustained dominant_tenant_share > 0.6.
- Phase 2 (selective demux): enable coarse demux for top 10 tenants by volume (protects hotspots) and re-validate.
- Phase 3: either flip fully unified or keep hybrid, depending on cost math.
aj: What about backfills? If attribution is delayed we need a deterministic replay path to re-attribute historical batches for billing. That implies stable keys + replay id.
kevin: Replay id already exists (trace_id-based). We need to ensure enrichers are idempotent and we persist mapping results long enough for backfill windows (30 days?).
sophia: SLOs to watch for rollout: batch latency p99, per-tenant token billing lag, attribution mismatch rate, GPU utilization delta vs baseline.
tarun: Ops alerts to add:
- high dominant_tenant_share (>0.5 sustained 5m)
- attribution_mismatch_rate > 0.5%
- batch_replay_failures > 0
maria: OK owners:
- canary deploy + metrics: aj
- attribution validator (back-test): kevin
- hotspot rules & coarse demux policy: sophia
- replay/backfill infra: tarun
aj: I'll schedule the canary for Thursday 10:00 PT. Will post the deploy job link.
kevin: For the validator, I need a sample comparator that compares per-tenant cost in old pipeline vs new. Quick pseudo:
```
old_cost = sum(tokens * old_unit_cost_per_tenant)
new_cost = sum(tokens * new_unit_cost_allocation)
mismatch = abs(old_cost - new_cost) / old_cost
```
maria: Keep sampled payloads anonymized — strip prompt tokens before storing. Use the existing sample-store retention policy.
sophia: One more tradeoff note: unified batcher increases variance in per-tenant latency due to batching blend. We might need per-tenant latency SLAs for enterprise tenants -> then demuxing becomes a stronger requirement.
aj: Noted. We'll flag enterprise customers and optionally route them to dedicated queues in Dedicated mode.
ingest-bot: Canary deploy queued at 1787774450 for cluster eng-canary-3. Job: deploy/unified-batcher-canary
maria: Great. After canary we reconvene and decide whether to move to coarse-demux or continue tuning unified.
aj: Thanks team — I'll drop a short runbook in #eng-platform before the deploy. :thumbsup:
kevin: +1
sophia: :+1:
tarun: :rocket:
